status_summary: On 2025-03-21 EOIR reinstated its 2019 policy on status dockets (PM 25-27), and on 2025-04-18 its Acting Director issued PM 25-29, rescinding the 2021 memo on administrative closure and stating that no statute authorizes it, while noting the 2024 rule stayed binding until rescinded or vacated. On 2026-06-22 the Northern District of Texas entered a consent judgment in Texas v. DOJ declaring the 2024 EOIR docket rule contrary to law and vacating it, and, per an advocacy advisory, barring DOJ from rules allowing administrative closure without a statutory basis; on 2026-08-21 the court denied a motion by cities and a legal services group to intervene, and they appealed to the Fifth Circuit. The actions limit immigration judges' closure authority; ICE's own use of termination and closure motions was not shown to have changed by a written policy.

timeline.event: EOIR Acting Director Sirce Owen issued PM 25-29, rescinding Director's Memorandum 22-03 on administrative closure and stating that no statute authorizes administrative closure by EOIR adjudicators.

In Texas v. DOJ (N.D. Tex., No. 7:26-cv-00070) the court entered a consent judgment the same day the complaint was filed, declaring the 2024 EOIR docket management rule in excess of statutory authority, vacating it and, per an advocacy advisory, enjoining DOJ from rules allowing administrative closure without an express statutory basis; the parties waived appeal.
The district court denied a motion by Baltimore, Columbus, New Haven and Centro Legal de la Raza to intervene and defend the 2024 rule; the movants appealed to the Fifth Circuit.
